thread:
Alex: Hey team — seeing flaky SSE streams in Safari when users are behind our CDN. Streams start, produce a few events, then abruptly stop (partial output) and the client reconnects. Repro is consistent for Safari 16.x/macOS and iOS. We use cookie-based session auth (Set-Cookie on signin).
Rina: Thanks, Alex. Can you paste minimal repro steps + request/response headers? Also which CDN and any recent config changes?
Alex: Repro: open a new tab to our stream URL, EventSource in frontend: 
```
const s = new EventSource('/api/stream');
s.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
```
Server response headers (sample):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
Vary: Cookie
Set-Cookie: session=abc123; Path=/; HttpOnly
```
On subsequent reconnects I sometimes see 304 from the CDN. Client logs show connection closed with partial data, then reconnect.
Rina: CDN?
Alex: Fastly (via our infra). No recent change on our side other than a deploy a week ago.
Eli: Looking quickly — if CDN returns 304 for streamed endpoints or rewrites responses, browsers can interpret that as end-of-stream. Safari historically treats an unexpected EOF from EventSource as final and then triggers a reconnect that can lose some buffered KV cache behavior. The "Vary: Cookie" + caching policy looks suspicious. Also Set-Cookie on the SSE response is a red flag. SSE responses should generally be non-cacheable and shouldn't set cookies mid-stream.
Jon: I pulled edge traces for Alex's requests. Sequence: origin returns 200 with chunked SSE, CDN caches and then later returns 304 for follow-up GETs due to our cache headers. When edge serves a 304 it sometimes doesn't stream body bytes and closes the socket after headers — Safari sees that as truncated stream. Chrome tends to keep retrying and re-writes state differently which masks the issue.
Rina: Workarounds we can recommend to the customer while we investigate?
Jon: Short-term: 1) Disable caching for SSE endpoints (Cache-Control: no-store or Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate) 2) Remove Vary: Cookie on streaming responses so CDN won't attempt to cache based on cookies 3) Avoid setting Set-Cookie on the stream response 4) Prefer passing auth via Authorization header or short-lived query token for EventSource (or use fetch streaming with keepalive for browsers that support it). Also ensure CORS allows credentials if using Authorization cookie: Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and preflight allows Authorization header.
Alex: We can't immediately change auth flow across all clients. Is there something Redwood can change on hosted endpoints to reduce impact?
Jon: For hosted streams we can enforce non-cacheable headers for any response with Content-Type: text/event-stream. I'll queue a canary change to add `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and strip Vary/Set-Cookie for those endpoints. That should stop cdn 304s for SSE.
Eli: Also add an explicit CORS response for credentialed requests: `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type` — and ensure preflight passes.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for "sse-cache-fix" to 10% of instances.
Alex: Great — we'll test with our users on Fastly and let you know. Thanks. :thumbsup:
Rina: Also logging note — ask customers to include browser console logs and the edge request IDs if it happens again so we can match traces quickly.
Alex: Will do. If this fixes it for us, please leave a note in the incident list so others know the workaround.
Jon: I'll post a short follow-up in #eng-runtime once canary is healthy and then promote to 100%.
Alex: Closing for now, will reopen if we see recurrences. Thanks everyone!
